 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Ashutosh Kumar
 and
 Honourable Mr. Justice Rajesh Kumar Verma
Oral Order

(Per: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE ASHUTOSH KUMAR)
6 12-12-2024 We have heard Mr. Avinash Singh, the learned Advocate for the appellant/applicant and Mr. Ajay Mishra, the learned APP for the State.
2. The appellant seeks suspension of his sentence during the pendency of the appeal.
3. The written objection is on record.

Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.865 of 2024(6)
dt.12-12-2024 4.

The appellant has been convicted under Section 376(1) of the Indian Penal Code vide judgment dated 19.06.2024 passed by the learned Additional District & Sessions Judge-I, Patna in Sessions Ravikant @ Ravi Kant vs The State Of Bihar on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120518763/
1 Trial No. 387 of 2020 (C.I.S. No. 387 of 2020), arising out of Mahila P.S. Case No. 47 of 2019. By order dated 22.06.2024

sentences.text:
, he has been sentenced to undergo R.I. for twelve years, to pay a fine of Rs.
10,000/- and in default of payment of fine, to further suffer imprisonment for six months under Section 376(1) of the IPC.
5. Notice was issued to respondent No. 2/ prosecutrix.
The same was refused to be received by her mother.
6. An affidavit of jointness of the prosecutrix with her mother has also been filed by the appellant/applicant.
7. According to the accusation, the prosecutrix had developed relationship with the appellant while both of them were employed in a Dance school.
The appellant Patna High Court CR. APP (DB)
No.865 of 2024(6) dt.12-12-2024 was the Director of the School, whereas the prosecutrix gave dance lessons to the students.
They entered into physical relationship on a number of occasions.
The allegation is that the appellant had promised to marry the prosecutrix.
However, she learnt later that the marriage of the appellant has been fixed somewhere else.
She tried to reason out with the appellant, but he refused to abide by his promise to marry her.
She had also realized then that she had become pregnant.
8. Hence the case.

9. The learned counsel for the appellant has shown from the evidence of the prosecutrix (P.W. 2)
that the victim was married to somebody else and against her husband, she had filed a case under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code.
At the time when she had developed relationship with the appellant, her marriage with her husband subsisted.
There is also no proof of the victim having become pregnant or of her abortion later.
In fact, she claims to have given birth to a child, said to be Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.865 of 2024(6) dt.12-12-2024 fathered by the appellant.
10. This also could not be proved at the trial.
11. The narration of events by the prosecutrix in the written report as also in her deposition before the Trial Court do not make out a case of rape.
It is primarily a case of the appellant reneging on his promise to marry the prosecutrix.
12. Considering the entire fact scenario of the case, we are inclined to suspend the sentence of the appellant.
13. We order accordingly.

14. For the reasons afore-stated, the sentence of the appellant/applicant is suspended and he is directed to be released on bail, during the pendency of the appeal, on his furnishing bail bonds in sum of Rs. 10,000/- (ten thousand) with two sureties of like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Additional District & Sessions Judge-I, Patna, in connection with Sessions Trial No. 387 Ravikant @ Ravi Kant vs The State Of Bihar on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120518763/
